To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the individual up- (down-)quark contributions to the electromagnetic form factors of the proton and the neutron can be described in the framework of a relativistic constituent quark model with a good agreement to the recent experimental data.

the flavor decomposition of the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon is well described within our relativistic constituent-quarks model, and that this is a first step in a more comprehensive study of the role of quark degrees of freedom in the nucleon.

1) the flavor contributions to the proton and neutron magnetic moments are very well predicted by a simple quark-counting rule, 2) the proton and neutron electric form factors are well described by a simple constituent quark model, and 3) the flavor contributions are very well predicted in the momentum-transfer region of the form factors, $Q^2<3.5$ GeV$^4$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nucleon structure in terms of the quark-gluon degrees of freedom, and we find that a relativistic constituent quark model is able to provide an adequate description of the nucleon structure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the constituent-quark model provides a reasonable framework for the description of the nucleon electromagnetic properties in the intermediate momentum-transfer range.
the constituent-quark picture of the proton and the neutron is a good approximation for the description of their electromagnetic form factors in a wide kinematical range.
the constituent-quark model is a viable and useful tool for the description of nucleon electromagnetic properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flavor dependence of the form factors is rather weak, and the up- and down-quark contributions to the nucleonic electromagnetic form factors are almost equal.
the nucleon electromagnetic structure is a collective property of the up- and down-quark degrees of freedom and not a simple superposition of the individual quark form factors.
flavor decomposition of the nucleon electromagnetic properties can be used as a powerful tool to test the validity of theoretical approaches.
